justification: Finding [0] identifies exactly the known defect: "`part.match(_placeholderRe)` is true for any placeholder, not just hex escapes. SafeSelector also replaces attribute selectors (`[attr=x]`), `:nth-child(...)` arguments..." and that a following hex-looking character causes a real separator to be skipped, breaking scoping. Its suggested remedy ("limited to placeholders that stand for a hex escape") leads directly to the actual fix of giving escapes a distinct `__esc-ph-N__` placeholder. Finding [1] raises a different issue (the lookahead applies to non-space combinators like `+`/`~`), with an example (`.\fc+bar`) that is an escape case and remains unfixed by the actual commit; its suggested fix (restricting to space separators) would not address the shared-placeholder root cause (e.g. `[a] .b` would still break). It does not match.

Finding [0] identifies the exact faulty code (`part.match(_placeholderRe)`) and the exact mechanism: "SafeSelector also uses `__ph-N__` placeholders for attribute selectors such as `[hidden]` and for `:nth-child(...)` expressions. A real descendant combinator after one of these is then wrongly treated as an escape-terminating space whenever the next character is a hex digit." This is precisely the known bug — the placeholder check is too broad because attribute selectors share the same placeholder format. Acting on it (distinguishing escape placeholders from other placeholders) leads directly to the fix of introducing a separate `__esc-ph-N__` placeholder. The examples differ slightly (`[hidden] div` vs `:host[foo]>div`) but the defect and failure mechanism are the same.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: 'The `if (_global.beforeEach)` / `if (_global.afterEach)` guards were removed, so `beforeEach(...)` and `afterEach(...)` are now called unconditionally at module load... it now throws a ReferenceError' in test_hooks.ts when no test framework is present. Acting on it leads directly to restoring the guards, as the fix does with `globalThis.beforeEach?.(...)`. Finding [1] describes a similar mechanism but in a different file (platform-browser matchers.ts), which the fix does not touch; it is a different defect. Finding [2] concerns removal of the `ɵ_global` export from @angular/localize, unrelated to the known bug.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: the removal of the `if (_global.beforeEach)` / `if (_global.afterEach)` guards in test_hooks.ts so that `beforeEach(...)`/`afterEach(...)` are called unconditionally, and that "Importing `@angular/core/testing` where no test framework has defined these globals now throws a ReferenceError at module load" (e.g. in a bundler context). This is the same faulty code and failure mechanism as the fix, which restores the guard via `globalThis.beforeEach?.(...)`; acting on this finding would lead directly to that change.

Finding [0] targets the `isDefaultImport` helper's handling of combined imports (`import CmpA, {CmpB} from './x'`) and proposes changing the check to look at `importClause.name`. The known bug is different: `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport` is never set in `collectDeferredSymbols`, so the per-block defer deps function always emits `m.ComponentName` for pure default imports. The finding's suggested fix (altering the helper's logic) would leave the per-block flag unset and the bug in place; it describes a different (edge-case) defect, not the missing assignment.

The known bug is that `collectDeferredSymbols` populates `isDefaultImport` in the `deferrableTypes` map but never sets `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport`, so the per-block deps function always emits `m.SymbolName`. Finding [0] instead critiques the `isDefaultImport` helper's logic for mixed imports (`import CmpA, {Other} from './a'`), stating "the function returns false" because `namedBindings` is defined. That is a different defect: acting on it would change the helper's heuristic, not add the missing `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport = ...` assignment, and would leave the known bug in place for plain default imports.

Finding [0] claims the clause is 'inverted' and that 'links that don't depend on router state subscribe needlessly' — this diagnosis implies subscribing in fewer cases, which the known-bug description explicitly flags as a different defect; acting on it would leave relative links (e.g. queryParamsHandling='replace') with stale hrefs. Finding [1] points at the dead constructor call and the inverted `!this.isAnchorElement` check, with the mechanism 'an anchor that never gets ngOnChanges will never update its href'. That is a different failure mechanism from the real bug (the premise that only preserveFragment/merge/preserve links depend on router state is wrong, so relative links go stale after navigation); its suggested fix would move the constructor call but keep the conditional gating logic in place rather than removing it as the actual fix does. Neither finding identifies that the subscription condition itself is fundamentally wrong for relative links.

Finding [0] identifies the inverted constructor condition (`if (!isAnchorElement)`) and the resulting tabindex/subscription mix-up. While the fix does also restore that condition, acting on finding 0 would only swap the branches back; the conditional `subscribeToNavigationEventsIfNecessary` logic (which still runs from ngOnChanges) would remain, so relative links with e.g. `queryParamsHandling="replace"` would still have stale hrefs. It does not identify the real mechanism (the premise that href only depends on router state for preserveFragment/merge/preserve is wrong because relative links depend on the ActivatedRoute). Finding [1] says 'The subscription condition for default query params handling looks backwards' and that it 'skips subscribing when the global default is merge or preserve' — this is exactly the clause-inversion complaint the known bug description calls out as a different defect; its fix would subscribe in fewer cases, the opposite of the real fix which always subscribes for anchors. Neither finding matches.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the mechanism of the known bug: "An observable that completes without emitting used to resolve `undefined`, but now it rejects with `EmptyError`," and specifically cites `loadChildren` returning `EMPTY` now throwing "an unexpected `EmptyError`" instead of reaching the existing handling. This is the same faulty code (the firstValueFrom replacement used in recognize.ts) and the same failure mechanism (EmptyError surfacing where previously undefined/no-match was handled). A maintainer acting on it would examine how EmptyError propagates through recognize.ts and arrive at treating EmptyError as a non-match, equivalent to the fix. It also mentions a secondary first-vs-last value difference, but that does not detract from the core match.

Finding [0] describes exactly the known bug: "cancelLeavingNodes treats any leaving element in a different DOM parent as an overlay duplicate and force-removes it. `leavingNodes` is keyed by TNode, and a TNode is shared by every instance of a component or template... the leaving element is cancelled and removed immediately. Its leave animation is cut short even though it is not a duplicate." This identifies the same faulty code (the cross-parent branch in cancelLeavingNodes), the same root cause (TNode shared across instances), and the same failure (leave animation skipped for a distinct instance), which would lead a maintainer to the fix of distinguishing instances by declaration view. Finding [1] concerns stale entries/memory leak in trackLeavingNodes, a different issue. Finding [2] concerns removal of removeAnimationsFromQueue and enter-animation conflicts, unrelated to the known bug.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: "cancelLeavingNodes force-removes any leaving element under the same tNode whose parent differs... A tNode is shared by every instance of a template or component, so unrelated instances in different DOM parents share it... creating another instance elsewhere cancels the first one's leave animation and removes it from the DOM immediately." This is the same faulty code (the cross-parent branch in cancelLeavingNodes) and the same mechanism (TNode shared across distinct instances), which the fix addresses by tracking declaration views. Finding [1] concerns stale leavingNodes entries on the move/reorder path and the previousSibling branch — a different issue. Finding [2] concerns removed enter-animation dequeuing in node_animations.ts — unrelated to the known bug.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: it notes that `stringifyAndEscape(position)` changes the wire format from the comma-separated "0,1,2" to the JSON array string "[0,1,2]", that the backend's `findConstructorByPosition`/`findDomElementByPosition` still parse with `split(',').map(parseInt)`, and that "This diff does not change the receiving side, so the format change breaks both operations." This is the same faulty code, the same mechanism (wire format changed without updating the consumer), and acting on it would lead a maintainer to update the backend parser (the actual fix) or equivalently revert the format.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: it notes that `position` was previously interpolated as a comma-joined string, that `stringifyAndEscape` now sends "[0,1,2]", that the receiving functions parse with `split(',')`/`parseInt` and would get NaN, and explicitly states "The diff does not change the receiving side to JSON.parse the argument" — which is precisely what the fix does in component-tree.ts (`JSON.parse(serializedPosition)`). Same faulty lines, same mechanism, and its implied fix matches the actual fix.
